speaker: Unknown
en: Good morning, everyone.
zh: 大家早上好。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm Romain.
zh: 我是 Romain。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hey, everyone.
zh: 嘿，大家好。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm Alexander.
zh: 我是 Alexander。

speaker: Unknown
en: Wow, this room is incredible.
zh: 哇，这个房间太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's over 7,000 AI engineers here today with us.
zh: 今天这里有超过 7,000 名 AI 工程师和我们在一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's not just about who's talking about this technology.
zh: 这不仅仅关乎谁在谈论这项技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's also about who's actually using it and pushing the frontier every day.
zh: 也关乎谁在真正使用它并每天都在推动前沿。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we couldn't be more proud to be here with all of you today.
zh: 所以我们今天能和你们所有人在一起，感到无比自豪。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when we were thinking about this event with Alex, we kept coming back to the World's Fair.
zh: 当我和 Alex 策划这次活动时，我们一直在回味世界博览会。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the World's Fair made actually the future visible to everyone by building it in public.
zh: 世界博览会实际上通过公开建造，让未来对每个人可见。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ideas that previously sounded impossible were actually suddenly there.
zh: 以前听起来不可能的想法实际上突然出现了。

speaker: Unknown
en: People could see them, they could walk into them, and they could even start to believe in them.
zh: 人们可以看到它们，可以走进它们，甚至可以开始相信它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: And honestly, this event has the exact same energy.
zh: 老实说，这次活动有着完全相同的活力。

speaker: Unknown
en: The future of engineering is not arriving from somewhere else.
zh: 工程的未来并不是从别处来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's really being built here by the people in this room and much faster than most expected.
zh: 它实际上正在这里由这个房间里的人构建，而且比大多数人预期的要快得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's why it's a little surprising that people keep saying that engineers are going away.
zh: 所以有点令人惊讶的是，人们一直说工程师将要消失了。

speaker: Unknown
en: The argument is that coding is abstracted away, and therefore, eventually, we won't need engineers.
zh: 这种论点是编码被抽象掉了，因此最终我们将不需要工程师。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, in fact, we think it's quite the opposite.
zh: 嗯，事实上我们认为恰恰相反。

speaker: Unknown
en: Software ate the world, and then AI ate software.
zh: 软件吞噬了世界，然后 AI 吞噬了软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: But now, what we're here to say is that the AI engineers are eating the world.
zh: 但现在我们要说的是，AI 工程师正在吞噬世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: AI engineers are the people here pushing the frontier.
zh: AI 工程师是这里推动前沿的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you all are figuring out how this new capability can reach everyone.
zh: 你们所有人都在弄清楚这种新能力如何能够触达每个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there has never been a better time to be an engineer, in fact, because engineering was never about writing code.
zh: 事实上，成为工程师从来没有比现在更好的时机，因为工程从来不是关于编写代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: Engineering has always been about solving problems for yourself and for other people as well.
zh: 工程一直是关于为自己和他人解决问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's about taking the latest science and combining it with design, with taste, with judgment, and most of all, imagination to make something that people can actually use.
zh: 它是关于利用最新的科学，并将其与设计、品味、判断力，尤其是想象力结合起来，制造出人们真正可以使用的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in that sense, it's not the end of engineering.
zh: 从这个意义上说，这不是工程的终结。

speaker: Unknown
en: We think it's a return to the roots of engineering.
zh: 我们认为这是回归工程的本源。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the technology we're building on is accelerating, getting faster and faster.
zh: 我们正在构建的技术正在加速，变得越来越快。

speaker: Unknown
en: For example, we used to ship a new model every 15 months or so, and now it's about roughly every six weeks.
zh: 例如，我们过去每 15 个月左右发布一个新模型，现在大约每六周发布一次。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in case you missed it, last week we launched a preview of the 5.6 series, and we're super excited to get into all of your hands.
zh: 如果你错过了，上周我们发布了 5.6 系列的预览版，我们非常兴奋能让它交到你们所有人手中。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, building on top of all these models, the rate of product progress is relentless.
zh: 现在，基于所有这些模型，产品进步的节奏是无情的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as a result, I don't have to tell you, the engineering feels completely different.
zh: 结果是，不用我多说，工程感觉完全不同了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So just to go over a couple years of what for me were successive mind-blowing experiences.
zh: 所以回顾过去几年对我来说那是连续的令人大开眼界的经历。

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously for a long time we've had completion, and then we went to inline prediction, and then finally we had command K where you could ask a model to make a change, but they wouldn't test the work.
zh: 显然很长一段时间以来我们有了补全功能，然后我们转向了行内预测，最后我们有了 Command K，你可以要求模型进行更改，但它们不会测试工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then models started testing the work, and now we have models taking on long, hard goals until they're done.
zh: 然后模型开始测试工作，现在我们有了模型承担长期、艰巨的目标直到完成。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for me, each of these phases, I remember the first time was just mind-blowing, and then obviously afterwards you just get used to it and you're trying to get your work done.
zh: 对我来说，这些阶段中的每一个，我都记得第一次简直是令人大开眼界，但显然之后你就习惯了它，并且你试图完成你的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, in fact, I can't believe that build and test loop was not even part of the models just two years ago.
zh: 是的，事实上我不敢相信，构建和测试循环在两年前甚至还不是模型的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: This was a picture of me at Dev Day 2024, and I used O1 in preview at the time to build a mini drone interface from scratch.
zh: 这是我在 2024 年 Dev Day 上的一张照片，我当时使用了处于预览版的 O1 从零开始构建了一个微型无人机界面。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the slightly insane part is the model could not actually run the code or verify its own work.
zh: 稍微疯狂的部分是，模型实际上无法运行代码或验证自己的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: and I knew the demo would work most of the time, but surely not all of the time, so I had to cross my fingers.
zh: 我知道演示大部分时间都会奏效，但肯定不会一直奏效，所以我不得不祈祷一切顺利。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can kind of see here that I was pretty nervous, but hey, that's me.
zh: 你可以在这里看到我相当紧张，但是嘿，那就是我。

speaker: Unknown
en: I only do live demos, so I never know what's actually going to happen each time.
zh: 我只做现场演示，所以我从来不知道每次真正会发生什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Luckily, it did work, and by dev day of last year in 2025, I was confident enough now that the mouse could test their own work to kind of control an entire camera system and lighting system live, but yeah, we've come a long way.
zh: 幸运的是，它确实奏效了，到了去年 2025 年的开发者日，我现在有足够的信心鼠标可以测试他们自己的工作，从而现场控制整个摄像头系统和照明系统，但是是的，我们已经走了很长的路。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so we refer to Romain as the demo god, and before the demo,
zh: 是的，所以我们称 Romain 为演示之神，在演示之前，

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll ask him, so how often does demo work?
zh: 我会问他，那么演示多久能成功一次？

speaker: Unknown
en: He'll be like, you know, three times out of four.
zh: 他会像，你知道的，四次里有三次。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're like, all right, good luck.
zh: 我们就像，好吧，祝你好运。

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously, we've come miles since then.
zh: 显然，从那时起我们已经取得了巨大的进展。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this year alone has been crazy.
zh: 今年光是这一年就很疯狂。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what we're putting up here are all the things that we've shipped so far.
zh: 所以我们在这里展示的是我们到目前为止发布的所有东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Actually, not even all.
zh: 其实,并没有包含所有。

speaker: Unknown
en: A selection of the things that we've shipped so far this year.
zh: 这是我们今年发布的内容的一部分精选。

speaker: Unknown
en: My favorite things that we've shipped are like Codex app, goal mode, remote.
zh: 我最喜欢的我们发布的东西是 Codex app、goal mode、remote。

speaker: Unknown
en: these are things that really changes how it feels to do work.
zh: 这些东西真的改变了做工作的感觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously we couldn't do these things if we didn't use Codex to build Codex, but I think to me what is most interesting is that now Codex can do, and agents can do, any task that you can do on your own computer.
zh: 显然,如果我们不使用 Codex 来构建 Codex,我们就不可能做这些事情,但我认为对我来说最有趣的是,现在 Codex 可以做,而且智能体 可以做,任何你可以在自己的计算机上做的任务。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that means they're not just helping you with the coding, but they're helping you with what happens before the coding.
zh: 这意味着它们不仅帮助你进行编码,还帮助你处理编码前发生的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: and they're helping you with what happens after the coding.
zh: 并且它们帮助你处理编码后发生的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is really key, right?
zh: 这真的很关键,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there's been a lot of talk, there will be a lot of talk today about loops.
zh: 我想已经有很多讨论了,今天也会有很多关于循环 的讨论。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you can connect the agent to not only the work that you have to do, but why it has to be done, that's how you can get the agent to start to begin much more work.
zh: 如果你不仅将智能体连接到你必须做的工作,还连接到为什么要做这项工作,这就是你可以让智能体 开始开始更多工作的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then if you can connect it to what you do afterwards, review and deploy, that's how you help it land much more work.
zh: 然后,如果你可以将其与你之后做的事情联系起来,即审查和部署,这就是你帮助它落地更多工作的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: So with all of this, of course we can move much faster, but to me as a product person, the most exciting thing is actually that we make better decisions around what to build.
zh: 因此,有了这一切,当然我们可以快得多,但对我来说,作为一个产品人,最令人兴奋的事情实际上是我们在围绕构建什么做出更好的决策。

speaker: Unknown
en: For instance, we try, we prototype many more ideas, and we spend much more time with users.
zh: 例如,我们尝试,我们原型化更多的想法,而且我们花更多的时间与用户在一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: So yes, that's all of you.
zh: 是的,那就是你们所有人。

speaker: Unknown
en: So wanted to pause and just give you all a big thank you, both for the love and the constructive feedback.
zh: 所以想暂停一下,衷心感谢大家,感谢你们的爱和建设性的反馈。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would say it's safe to say that we, Codex, and actually the entire industry wouldn't be here without you.
zh: 我想说可以肯定地说,我们,Codex,实际上是整个行业,如果没有你们就不会在这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, thank you so much for all the feedback.
zh: 是的,非常感谢所有的反馈。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're constantly listening to all of you.
zh: 我们一直在倾听你们所有人的声音。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you.
zh: 谢谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: OK, so the models are getting really good.
zh: 好了,所以这些模型变得真的很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would say, if you pick a medium length computer task and you give me and the model the same amount of time to get that task done, probably, at least in my case, the model will do a better job than me for the average task.
zh: 我会说,如果你选择一个中等长度的计算机任务,并且给我和这些模型同样的时间来完成那个任务,可能,至少在我的情况中,对于普通任务模型会比我做得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, OK, we're getting these models.
zh: 所以,好了,我们正在得到这些模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: In some ways, they're smarter than us.
zh: 在某些方面,它们比我们更聪明。

speaker: Unknown
en: They can do almost anything.
zh: 它们几乎可以做任何事。

speaker: Unknown
en: How should we shape that?
zh: 我们应该如何塑造它?

speaker: Unknown
en: What should the products that we use feel like?
zh: 我们使用的产品应该感觉像什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: And so to answer that, we look to our mission.
zh: 为了回答这个问题,我们着眼于我们的使命。

speaker: Unknown
en: The part of it here that I've got up is AGI that benefits all of humanity.
zh: 我在这里展示的部分是造福全人类的 AGI。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think in order to do this, there are two main questions that I think about now.
zh: 我认为为了做到这一点,我现在主要考虑两个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is, how do we set up the agents to actually do things in the world?
zh: 一个是,我们如何设置智能体 在世界上实际做事情?

speaker: Unknown
en: So what can they do?
zh: 所以它们能做什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Gradually, agents are getting connected to more and more things.
zh: 逐渐地,智能体正被连接到越来越多的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then where do they run?
zh: 然后它们在哪里运行?

speaker: Unknown
en: More on that later.
zh: 稍后再详细说。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the other question is, how do we use these agents?
zh: 然后另一个问题是,我们要如何使用这些智能体?

speaker: Unknown
en: For us, what should the product feel like around them?
zh: 对于我们,围绕它们的产品感觉应该是什么样的?

speaker: Unknown
en: And for us, the goal is squarely not to automate engineers.
zh: 对于我们,目标绝对不是自动化工程师。

speaker: Unknown
en: Instead, the product shape that we want is one that maximally empowers engineers.
zh: 相反,我们想要的产品形态是最大限度地赋予工程师力量的形态。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if we think about what that product shape is, we actually think it's pretty simple.
zh: 所以如果我们考虑那种产品形态是什么,我们实际上认为这很简单。

speaker: Unknown
en: I read a lot of sci-fi and watch superhero movies, and I actually think that the simple ideas in there are approximately right.
zh: 我读很多科幻小说并看超级英雄电影,我实际上认为里面的简单想法大致是正确的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there are two modalities, roughly.
zh: 所以主要有两种模式,大致来说。

speaker: Unknown
en: Chat, I actually think, I know some people think chat is dead, I think chat is underrated.
zh: 聊天,我实际上认为,我知道有些人认为聊天已死,我认为聊天被低估了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And some kind of hands-on experience.
zh: 以及某种动手体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what you want is a single entity that you can ask for help with anything, anywhere.
zh: 所以你想要的是你可以随时随地寻求帮助的单一实体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you want a powerful collaborative UI that you can use when you want to inspect, steer, or shape things yourself.
zh: 然后你想要一个强大的协作 UI,当你想自己检查、引导或塑造事物时可以使用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I had Codex ImageGen me an illustration of this to help understand when you might want to use these things.
zh: 所以我让 Codex ImageGen 为我生成了一张插图来帮助理解你可能想要何时使用这些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so my analogy for you, yeah, I hope you like the ImageGen, my analogy for you would be it's just like working with a team.
zh: 所以我给你的类比,是的,我希望你喜欢 ImageGen,我给你的类比就是就像与团队一起工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Most of the time, you're just talking about stuff, and your team is just doing stuff.
zh: 大多数时候,你们只是在谈论事情,而你的团队只是在做事。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't actually want to watch over the shoulder or have to walk over to the workbench of your teammate for every single unit of work.
zh: 你其实不想一直盯着别人的肩膀，或者为了每一个单一的工作单元都要走到队友的工作台去。

speaker: Unknown
en: Mostly, you just want to talk and let them cook.
zh: 大多数时候，你只是想聊聊，然后让他们自己发挥。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then every now and then, you want to dig in and really dig in all the way to the weeds of things and dig into that problem together.
zh: 然后偶尔，你想要深入研究，真正深入到事物的细枝末节，一起钻研那个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for us, as we build product, we have this idea that we want to make it so that you can retain this feeling of mastery of the work that we're doing because that's really powerful.
zh: 对我们来说，当我们构建产品时，我们有这样一个想法，我们要让你能够保持对我们所做工作的掌控感，因为那是非常强大的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't want to make it feel like actually it's really hard to get to the details and disassemble the hardware in this case.
zh: 我们不想让它感觉起来，真的很难接触到细节并在这种情况下拆解硬件。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the way that we're bringing this to life is just the beginning, but this is why we built the Codex app.
zh: 所以我们要把这一点变为现实的方式才刚刚开始，但这就是我们构建 Codex 应用的原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: You get a very simple chat interface that you can use for coding and for anything else, and you can have a conversation and then go as deep as you want.
zh: 你会得到一个非常简单的聊天界面，你可以把它用于编码和其他任何事情，你可以进行对话，然后想多深入就可以多深入。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in the case here, we have Romain's predicted score of this upcoming World Cup match.
zh: 所以在这个例子里，我们有 Romain 对这场即将到来的世界杯比赛的预测比分。

speaker: Unknown
en: I hope I'm right.
zh: 我希望我是对的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I hope I'm right, we'll see.
zh: 我希望我是对的，我们拭目以待。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, and what you can do here is you can go in and you can point at a very specific thing and say, hey, I want you to make this change, or you can make this change yourself.
zh: 好的，你在这里可以做的就是你可以进入并指向一个非常具体的东西，然后说，嘿，我想让你做这个改动，或者你可以自己做这个改动。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a fun story here is that actually, I remember pitching some of you who I know are in the audience this idea before we started, and I was told squarely, like, I will never use such a tool.
zh: 这里有一个有趣的故事，其实我记得在我们开始之前，我向在座的一些人推销过这个想法，而且我被直接告知，比如，我永远不会使用这样的工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: I will never leave my terminal, or Vim or Emacs.
zh: 我永远不会离开我的终端，或者 Vim 或 Emacs。

speaker: Unknown
en: But actually those people are now using it.
zh: 但实际上那些人现在正在使用它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And even internally, like within our team,
zh: 甚至在内部，就像在我们的团队里，

speaker: Unknown
en: There were a lot of questions, like why should we build this?
zh: 当时有很多问题，比如我们为什么要构建这个？

speaker: Unknown
en: People love the CLI, they love the IDE, and it's a little subtle, but our take is that you can't really build that collaborative interface for any kind of work in a CLI.
zh: 人们喜欢 CLI，他们喜欢 IDE，这有点微妙，但我们的看法是，你无法真正在 CLI 中为任何类型的工作构建那种协作界面。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's mostly chat.
zh: 它主要是聊天。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then in an IDE, the order is wrong, so you're starting with the code, but now it's time to transition to working with teammates where you chat first and you dig in when you need it.
zh: 然后在 IDE 中，顺序是错误的，所以你是从代码开始的，但现在是时候转向与队友合作了，在这种情况下你要先聊天，在需要的时候再深入钻研。

speaker: Unknown
en: Totally.
zh: 完全同意。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're moving really fast on this, on the product surface and the model layer, of course.
zh: 我们在这方面进展非常快，在产品表面和模型层，当然。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we're also trying to keep pace with all of you.
zh: 但我们也正努力跟上你们所有人的步伐。

speaker: Unknown
en: Honestly, half the time I open X, I see someone in this room doing something that I had not realized Codex could actually do.
zh: 老实说，我有一半的时间打开 X，我看到这个房间里的人在做一些我没想到 Codex 竟然能做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And honestly, this is what pioneers do.
zh: 老实说，这就是先驱者所做的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You guys experiment.
zh: 你们进行实验。

speaker: Unknown
en: You set up tools for yourself, for your team.
zh: 你们为自己、为团队建立工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in turn, we get inspired.
zh: 反过来，我们要到了启发。

speaker: Unknown
en: We learn from you.
zh: 我们向你们学习。

speaker: Unknown
en: And eventually, everyone benefits.
zh: 最终，每个人都受益。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you are helping us figure out what to build next and also what the future of engineering should look like.
zh: 所以你们正在帮助我们弄清楚接下来要构建什么，以及工程未来的样子应该是什么样的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But for that to work, one thing that we really care about is that Codex cannot be a closed product that only OpenAI can improve.
zh: 但为了实现这一点，我们真正关心的一件事是，Codex 不能是一个只有 OpenAI 才能改进的封闭产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we've intentionally designed Codex as a set of layers that anyone can build on.
zh: 所以我们有意地将 Codex 设计为一组任何人都可以在其上构建的层级。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we want to show you a little bit of that stack today and how it manifests.
zh: 我们今天想向你们展示一点点那个技术栈以及它是如何呈现的。

speaker: Unknown
en: First, it starts with the model.
zh: 首先，它从模型开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Alexander showed how quickly we're progressing on models.
zh: Alexander 展示了我们在模型上进展得有多快。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you guys use these models through the responses API.
zh: 你们通过响应 API 使用这些模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And guess what?
zh: 猜猜怎么着？

speaker: Unknown
en: This is how we build the Codex app, right?
zh: 这就是我们构建 Codex 应用的方式，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: We use the same models through the same API.
zh: 我们通过相同的 API 使用相同的模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we actually are building on the same thing that we give to developers.
zh: 我们实际上是在构建与我们给开发者的相同的东西之上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when Codex needs something new, we always try to bake it into the API first so you can benefit as well.
zh: 当 Codex 需要新东西时，我们总是尝试先将其烘焙到 API 中，这样你们也能受益。

speaker: Unknown
en: One example recently was compaction.
zh: 最近的一个例子是压缩。

speaker: Unknown
en: Codex needed a way to compact long contexts for long-running tasks, and so we built that into the API.
zh: Codex 需要一种方法来压缩长时间运行任务的冗长上下文，所以我们把它构建到了 API 中。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that means your agents can use the same primitives that we built for ourselves.
zh: 所以这意味着你的智能体可以使用我们为自己构建的相同原语。

speaker: Unknown
en: Moving on to the next layer, the Codex harness is also open source.
zh: 进入下一层，Codex harness 也是开源的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you can inspect it, you can fork it, you can adapt it.
zh: 所以你可以检查它，你可以派生它，你可以调整它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we also took the same approach with AgentsMD.
zh: 我们对 AgentsMD 也采用了同样的方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Instead of reinventing a new file format for Codex to follow instructions, we thought, let's pick a name that other agents can actually use as well.
zh: 我们没有为 Codex 发明一种新的文件格式来遵循指令，而是想，让我们选一个其他智能体实际上也能使用的名字。

speaker: Unknown
en: The models are the default in the harness, the models from OpenAI, but they are not hard-coded in there.
zh: 这些模型是 harness 中的默认，来自 OpenAI 的模型，但它们并没有硬编码在那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you want to use an open model and keep the same agent loop, you can.
zh: 所以如果你想使用一个开放模型并保持相同的智能体循环，你可以。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we also bring this Codex harness into the post-training process of our model.
zh: 我们也将这个 Codex harness 引入到了我们模型的后训练过程中。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that means the models can learn to call tools and navigate an environment that's actually something that's open source.
zh: 这意味着模型可以学习调用工具并导航一个实际上是开源的环境。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now take the open code team for instance.
zh: 现在以 open code 团队为例。

speaker: Unknown
en: They actually were able to inspect how we have this reference implementation and they could reuse the parts that make sense to them or change entirely all the rest and make different choices.
zh: 他们实际上能够检查我们是如何拥有这个参考实现的，并且他们可以重用对他们有意义的部分，或者完全改变其余部分并做出不同的选择。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know for instance they were trying to see how we did sign in with ChatGPT and so they could look at the code and learn from it.
zh: 我知道例如他们正试图看我们是如何做通过 ChatGPT 登录的，这样他们就可以查看代码并从中学习。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we think it's better than having developers reverse engineering how it builds and how we launch.
zh: 我们认为这比让开发者去逆向工程它是如何构建的以及我们是如何发布的要好。

speaker: Unknown
en: But now let's say, speaking of subscriptions, that we want to go a level higher.
zh: 但现在假设，说到订阅，我们想要再提高一个层次。

speaker: Unknown
en: And how do you bring this harness into an app?
zh: 你如何将这个 harness 带入到一个应用程序中？

speaker: Unknown
en: And how do you let people sign in with their existing Codex subscription, for instance?
zh: 以及你如何让人们使用他们现有的 Codex 订阅登录，例如？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, it turns out we had the same problem ourselves, because we wanted to build a VS Code extension and the Codex app.
zh: 结果表明我们自己也有同样的问题，因为我们想要构建一个 VS Code 扩展和 Codex 应用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we wanted to have a unified way to actually control this harness.
zh: 而我们想要有一个统一的方式来实际控制这个 harness。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we built AppServer, and we also made that open source.
zh: 所以我们构建了 AppServer，并且我们也将其开源了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the app server is not kind of a community adapter.
zh: 而 app server 并不是那种社区适配器。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's really the path that we use for our own products.
zh: 它确实是我们自己产品所使用的路径。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can use it too.
zh: 你也可以使用它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thomas, for instance, here, aka Dimalian on X, he built his own native app for Codex called Codex Monitor before we even launched the Codex app.
zh: Thomas，例如这里的这位，在 X 上的也叫 Dimalian，他在我们甚至还没有发布 Codex 应用之前，就为 Codex 构建了他自己的名为 Codex Monitor 的原生应用。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because he could build that using the app server.
zh: 因为他可以使用 app server 来构建它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now he works on our team and he actually builds Codex for iOS.
zh: 现他在我们的团队工作，他实际上为 iOS 构建 Codex。

speaker: Unknown
en: And moving up the stack at the app layer, we also want to make sure that innovation is not blocked on our own ideas.
zh: 向上移动到应用层的堆栈，我们还要确保创新不会被我们自己的想法所阻挡。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we build extensible primitives here, like the in-app browser that we showed on the screen and plugins.
zh: 所以我们在这里构建了可扩展的原语，比如我们在屏幕上展示的浏览器内和插件。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you take, for instance, browser use and computer use, these were built as plugins using the same extension points that we have available for all of you.
zh: 所以如果你以浏览器使用和计算机使用为例，这些是使用我们提供给所有人的相同扩展点构建的插件。

speaker: Unknown
en: And lastly, we also recently built role-specific plugins for Codex, say, to make it easier to customize for people who work in data science or design, for instance.
zh: 最后，我们最近还为 Codex 构建了特定角色的插件，比如说，为了让那些在数据科学或设计工作的人更容易进行定制。

speaker: Unknown
en: And these plugins are also open source.
zh: 而这些插件也是开源的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can see under the hood and get inspired from them if that's useful.
zh: 如果有用的话，你可以看到底层并从中获得灵感。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our goal is really to keep making this as open and flexible as we can.
zh: 我们的目标确实是继续使这个尽可能开放和灵活。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the best part is people can use their existing subscription in more and more places, from OpenCode, Py, Droid, OpenClaw, to even Xcode and JetBrains as IDEs.
zh: 最棒的是，人们可以在越来越多的地方使用他们现有的订阅，从 OpenCode、Py、Droid、OpenClaw，甚至到 Xcode 和 JetBrains 这样的 IDE。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can see how they're becoming quite a meaningful part of how people use these tools.
zh: 你可以看到它们正在成为人们使用这些工具的方式中相当有意义的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's really why we want to care about building this open ecosystem with all of you.
zh: 这就是为什么我们要与你们所有人一起构建这个开放生态系统的真正原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: So really, if there's one thing I want you to take away from this section and this stack, it's this.
zh: 所以真的，如果有一件事我希望你们从这一节和这个堆栈中带走，那就是这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're not building one system for open AI and a second system that's simplified for developers.
zh: 我们不是为 open AI 构建一个系统，然后为开发者构建第二个简化了的系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: At every layer, we actually use the thing that we give to you.
zh: 在每一层，我们实际上都使用我们提供给你们的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we want to thank all of you because every time you fork the harness, every time you find the edge of capabilities of the models, it means we get to learn and improve.
zh: 我们想要感谢你们所有人，因为每当你们 fork 这个 harness，每当你们发现模型能力的边缘，这意味着我们要学习和改进。

speaker: Unknown
en: And honestly, with 7,000 of the finest AI engineers in this room today, I'm confident that all of you will define a lot of how we will experience AI and how the world will experience AI in the future.
zh: 坦率地说，今天在这个房间里坐着 7000 名最优秀的 AI 工程师，我有信心你们所有人将定义我们在未来如何体验 AI 以及世界将如何体验 AI 的很大一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: So thank you.
zh: 所以谢谢你们。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to give a shout out to whoever over there is injecting energy.
zh: 我想给那边正在注入能量的人点个名。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's you.
zh: 那就是你。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you so much.
zh: 非常感谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: So with all of your help, we are making agents explosively useful.
zh: 所以在你们所有人的帮助下，我们正在使智能体爆炸式地有用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so now the question is, how do we get value out of them?
zh: 所以现在的問題是，我们要如何从它们身上获得价值？

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's not token maxing.
zh: 而这并不是 token maxing。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have a term for this that maybe you use as well.
zh: 我们有一个这方面的术语，也许你们也用。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know.
zh: 我不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it on screen?
zh: 它在屏幕上吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Value maxing.
zh: Value maxing。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when we talk to engineering leaders, most of the conversation is about some themes relating to the idea of value maxing.
zh: 所以当我们与工程负责人交谈时，大部分对话是关于与 value maxing 这个想法相关的一些主题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we're gonna walk you through a few common topics that come up, some things where we've already made a lot of progress, and some things where actually there's a lot more progress to still be made.
zh: 所以我们将带你们了解几个出现的常见话题，一些是我们已经取得很多进展的事情，还有一些是实际上仍有更多进展要做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the first one of these is cost efficiency.
zh: 所以其中第一个是成本效率。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone wants frontier intelligence.
zh: 每个人都想要前沿智能。

speaker: Unknown
en: Pick your favorite eval, you want the best model.
zh: 挑选你最喜欢的评估，你想要最好的模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: So with terminal bench here, for instance, that's GPT 5.6 Sol, and like I said, we can't wait for you to have it.
zh: 所以这里的 terminal bench，就是 GPT 5.6 Sol，就像我说的，我们迫不及待想让你们拥有它。

speaker: Unknown
en: But okay, you also want as much intelligence as you can get, and that's where efficiency comes in.
zh: 但是好吧，你也想要尽可能多的智能，这就是效率发挥作用的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: Cost efficiency has been a focus for us for quite some time, and the results are continuing to pay off.
zh: 成本效率很长一段时间以来一直是我们的关注重点，结果也在持续回报。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for example, GPT 5.6 Terra, I think it's in like dark blue in there, brings GPT 5.5 level intelligence, but at half the cost.
zh: 比如说，GPT 5.6 Terra，我记得它在那里面是深蓝色的，带来了 GPT 5.5 级别的智能，但只需一半的成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Luna there beat some pretty notable models in this eval, but at only $1 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens.
zh: 而且 Luna 在这项评估中击败了一些非常著名的模型，但每百万输入 Token 只需 1 美元，每百万输出 Token 只需 6 美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll leave it up to you to compare those costs, but that is insane value.
zh: 我把比较这些成本的任务交给你，但这价值简直是疯了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, we really can't wait to see all of you build with GPT-5.6 and these new family of models.
zh: 是的，我们真的迫不及待想看到大家用 GPT-5.6 和这一系列新模型来构建。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, the next thing I want to touch on is speed, right?
zh: 现在，我想提到的下一件事是速度，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: GPT-5.3 Codec Spark showed you what speed can unlock.
zh: GPT-5.3 Codec Spark 向你们展示了速度能解锁什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we also know that you all want frontier intelligence.
zh: 但我们也知道你们都想要前沿智能。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't want to have a model that's not as great as what you can operate at the very best.
zh: 你不想要一个不如你能在最优状态下运作的那么好的模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, this is GPT 5.6 Sol running on Cerebras, the frontier intelligence at now 750 tokens a second.
zh: 好的，这是运行在 Cerebras 上的 GPT 5.6 Sol，前沿智能，现在每秒 750 个 Token。

speaker: Unknown
en: We can't wait to see what you can build with this next month.
zh: 我们迫不及待想看到下个月你能用它构建什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And honestly, to put that in perspective, this is kind of like having a pretty substantial PR written in like 10 seconds.
zh: 坦白说，为了让大家有个概念，这就像是在大概 10 秒内写好一篇相当实质性的 PR。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's not just about getting one answer faster, right?
zh: 而且这不仅仅是为了更快地得到一个答案，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's about what can you do with that speed?
zh: 而是关于你能用那个速度做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: You can think about an agent taking different approaches, maybe like five or six in parallel, maybe like coming back and picking the best one in the time it would have taken to not even generate just one.
zh: 你可以想象一个智能体采用不同的方法，也许五六个并行，也许在甚至还没来得及生成仅仅一个的时间里回来并挑选最好的那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we really can't wait to see what that can unlock when you have frontier intelligence, the very best at that speed.
zh: 所以当我们拥有前沿智能——那种最高级别的速度时，我们真的迫不及待想看到这能解锁什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: It really starts to feel less like waiting for an AI to respond and much more like a coworker that's already showing you the results as it goes.
zh: 这真的开始感觉没那么像是在等待 AI 回应，而更像是一个已经在向你展示结果的同事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Speaking of working with coworkers, can I get a show of hands?
zh: 说到与同事共事，能举个手吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Who is familiar with this kind of site in offices?
zh: 谁熟悉办公室里的这种站点？

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, okay, wow, a lot of you are very well behaved as I see some people up front.
zh: 好的，好的，哇，你们很多人都很守规矩，因为我看到前排有一些人。

speaker: Unknown
en: So yeah, a lot of people are keeping their laptops open so that agents can keep working.
zh: 所以是的，很多人让笔记本电脑保持开着，这样智能体就可以继续工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is funny, but what we really want is to be able to shut our computers and we wanna be able to run many tasks in parallel, isolated on their own box.
zh: 这很有趣，但我们真正想要的是能够关掉我们的电脑，并且我们想要能够在隔离的盒子里并行运行许多任务。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, we've been actually aiming at this from the start.
zh: 现在，我们实际上从一开始就以此为目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our first major launch was Codex Cloud, and it is due for some major upgrades coming soon.
zh: 我们的第一次重大发布是 Codex Cloud，而且它很快会有一些重大升级。

speaker: Unknown
en: But better yet, as we think about this, the future shouldn't have this awkward distinction between a local task and a cloud task, and you have to decide where to run everything.
zh: 但更好的是，当我们思考这个问题时，未来不应该有本地任务和云任务之间这种尴尬的区分，你必须决定在哪里运行所有东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: really what you should have is kind of going back to what I was saying earlier.
zh: 你真正应该拥有的有点像回到我之前所说的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You should just have an agent, you talk to it wherever, whenever, about anything, and it should figure out, okay, what do I need to do, which environment is right for my work, and use whatever is available.
zh: 你应该只有一个智能体，随时随地与它谈论任何事情，它应该弄清楚，好的，我需要做什么，哪个环境适合我的工作，并使用任何可用的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: In fact, Theo made this prediction over the weekend on this very topic, and it's a pretty acute tweet.
zh: 事实上，Theo 周末就这个话题做了预测，这是一条非常敏锐的推文。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, Alex, what do you think?
zh: 比如，Alex，你怎么看？

speaker: Unknown
en: Sooner or later than six months?
zh: 比六个月更早还是更晚？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think maybe not the exact details, but the vibe of this tweet, much sooner than six months.
zh: 我认为可能不是确切细节，但这推文的感觉，比六个月早得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, at the pace at which everything is going, I would not be surprised if it's sooner indeed.
zh: 我是说，以现在的进展速度，如果确实更早我也不会惊讶。

speaker: Unknown
en: You might be wondering, where is the live demo today?
zh: 你可能想知道，今天的现场演示在哪里？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, for this AI engineer, we wanted to do something a little different this time around.
zh: 嗯，对于这个 AI 工程师，我们这次想做点不一样的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we think it's a very unique moment for all of us to reimagine how we work and how we build.
zh: 我们认为这对我们要重新想象如何工作和如何构建来说是一个非常独特的时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we wanted to bring a special guest who has been to what's possible with agents and really has pushed us to be more AGI-pilled at OpenAI.
zh: 所以我们想带来一位特别嘉宾，他见证了智能体的可能性，并真的推动了我们在 OpenAI 更倾向于 AGI。

speaker: Unknown
en: So with that, please welcome to the stage the claw father, Peter Steinberger.
zh: 有了这个，请欢迎这位 Claw Father，Peter Steinberger 登台。

speaker: Unknown
en: Peter, take it away.
zh: Peter，交给你了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you all.
zh: 谢谢大家。

speaker: Unknown
en: Good morning, everyone.
zh: 大家早上好。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, I love this picture because it reminds me just how much has changed in a few months.
zh: 你知道，我喜欢这张图片，因为它提醒我几个月以来改变了多少。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was juggling 10 or more terminal windows.
zh: 我当时在管理 10 个或更多终端窗口。

speaker: Unknown
en: always waiting for one of them to finish so I could steal the agent and queue new work.
zh: 总是在等待其中一个完成，这样我就可以占用那个智能体并将新工作排队。

speaker: Unknown
en: In January, that felt like peak productivity.
zh: 在一月，那感觉像是生产力巅峰。

speaker: Unknown
en: Today, it feels a little bit silly.
zh: 今天，这感觉有点傻。

speaker: Unknown
en: I thought I was orchestrating.
zh: 我以为我在编排。

speaker: Unknown
en: Really, I was polling.
zh: 实际上，我在轮询。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was the scheduler, the router, and the memory.
zh: 我是调度器，是路由器，也是内存。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, at first, I paired with one agent.
zh: 你知道，起初，我与一个智能体结对。

speaker: Unknown
en: With 10 terminals, I was no longer pairing.
zh: 有了 10 个终端，我不再结对编程了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was managing 10 direct reports.
zh: 我在管理 10 个直属下属。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, I mostly talk to a long-running manager, which delegates work to a team.
zh: 现在，我主要和一个长期运行的管理者对话，它把工作委托给一个团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: For tricky work, I can still drop down and pair directly with a worker.
zh: 对于棘手的工作，我仍然可以降级并与一个工作者直接结对。

speaker: Unknown
en: But my default changed.
zh: 但我的默认方式改变了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I managed the manager of a small company of agents.
zh: 我管理着一个小型智能体公司的管理者。

speaker: Unknown
en: Three changes made that possible.
zh: 三个变化让这成为可能。

speaker: Unknown
en: Number one, server-side compaction made long-running tasks reliable enough that I stopped optimizing around fresh sessions.
zh: 第一，服务器端压缩让长期任务足够可靠，我不再围绕新会话进行优化。

speaker: Unknown
en: Coordination lets one thread create and steer the right projects.
zh: 协调让一个线程能创建并引导正确的项目。

speaker: Unknown
en: And third, automation can wake the same manager when something happens.
zh: 第三，自动化可以在事情发生时唤醒同一个管理者。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we have persistent context, delegation, and triggers.
zh: 所以我们要有持久化上下文、委托和触发器。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's your loop.
zh: 这就是你的循环。

speaker: Unknown
en: And once the loop starts working, you discover the next problem.
zh: 一旦循环开始运转，你就会发现下一个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: The bottleneck keeps moving.
zh: 瓶颈一直在移动。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, last year, I was primarily constrained by tokens.
zh: 你知道，去年，我主要受限于 tokens。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now I fixed that by joining OpenAI.
zh: 现在我通过加入 OpenAI 修复了这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know, I know, this strategy does not scale.
zh: 我知道，我知道，这种策略无法扩展。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then, my constraint shifted to token, uh, compute.
zh: 然后，我的约束转移到了 token，呃，计算。

speaker: Unknown
en: All these threads run at the same time and my MacBook starts sounding like a jet engine.
zh: 所有这些线程同时运行，我的 MacBook 开始听起来像喷气发动机。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's mostly fixed by using test boxes, so agents can run tests on a separate machine.
zh: 这主要通过使用测试盒修复了，所以智能体可以在单独的机器上运行测试。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, I'm primarily constrained by attention.
zh: 现在，我主要受限于注意力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And unlike tokens or compute, I can't simply add more of it.
zh: 与 tokens 或计算不同，我不能简单地增加更多的注意力。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the most important skill
zh: 所以今天最重要的技能

speaker: Unknown
en: is today is deciding where to spend it.
zh: 是决定把注意力花在哪里。

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you still staring at the agent while the code flies by?
zh: 当代码飞速闪过时，你还在盯着智能体看吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I know it feels cool, but with the earlier models, this was necessary.
zh: 我知道这感觉很酷，但对于早期的模型，这是必要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You see the agent go in a direction you don't like, you hit escape, you steer it, you steer it back.
zh: 你看到智能体朝你不喜欢方向发展，你按下 escape，你引导它，你把它引导回来。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the latest generation of models is so good at understanding intent that it's a little bit of a waste of time to watch the agent generate code.
zh: 但最新一代的模型非常擅长理解意图，看着智能体生成代码有点浪费时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: Imagine someone files an issue on one of my open source projects.
zh: 想象有人在我的开源项目之一上提了一个 issue。

speaker: Unknown
en: The manager wakes up, reads it against the project's goals, notes, and vision, and decides whether it might be a fit.
zh: 管理者醒来，对照项目目标、笔记和愿景阅读它，并决定它是否可能合适。

speaker: Unknown
en: If it does, it creates a workout.
zh: 如果合适，它创建一个 workout。

speaker: Unknown
en: That worker investigates, implements the change, runs the tests, and another agent can review the result.
zh: 那个工作者调查、实施变更、运行测试，另一个智能体可以审查结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't need to watch those agents work or consume every intermediary message.
zh: 我不需要看那些智能体工作或消费每一个中间消息。

speaker: Unknown
en: When the manager needs me, it returns a PR, the original issue, the proposed diff, maybe a video or even a running build I can VNC into.
zh: 当管理者需要我时，它返回一个 PR、原始 issue、提议的 diff，也许还有一个视频，甚至一个我可以 VNC 进入的运行构建。

speaker: Unknown
en: I review once.
zh: 我审查一次。

speaker: Unknown
en: I leave a note, I maybe approve, the loop continues and it can land after the checks pass.
zh: 我留个言，我也许批准，循环继续，它可以在检查通过后落地。

speaker: Unknown
en: The agent runs the inner execution loop.
zh: 智能体运行内部执行循环。

speaker: Unknown
en: I set the direction and I make decisions in the outer loop.
zh: 我设定方向，我在外部循环中做决策。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, Paul Salt is already running a version of this.
zh: 你知道，Paul Salt 已经在运行这个的一个版本了。

speaker: Unknown
en: He pinned his chief of staff, it wakes up every 10 minutes and it coordinates his GitHub work.
zh: 他固定了他的幕僚长，它每 10 分钟醒来一次，并协调他的 GitHub 工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: The agent creates threads in the sidebar so Paul can jump in whenever the work needs additional steering.
zh: 智能体在侧边栏创建线程，这样 Paul 可以在工作需要额外引导时随时跳入。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, once the manager is long-lived, tying it to a laptop just feels wrong.
zh: 你知道，一旦管理者是长期存活的，把它绑定到笔记本电脑上感觉就是错的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Codecs can already move work between hosts.
zh: Codecs 已经可以在主机之间移动工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: OpenClaw has a gateway and nodes.
zh: OpenClaw 有一个网关和节点。

speaker: Unknown
en: But neither feels like the final form.
zh: 但两者都不像是最终形态。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't even want to think where I work.
zh: 我甚至不想想我在哪里工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: My agent should be able to connect to any of my machines.
zh: 我的智能体应该能够连接到我的任何机器。

speaker: Unknown
en: They should know which work can be done in the cloud or which work requires my local machine.
zh: 它们应该知道哪些工作可以在云中完成，或者哪些工作需要我的本地机器。

speaker: Unknown
en: The manager shouldn't be a session trapped inside your app.
zh: 管理者不应该是一个被困在你的应用里的会话。

speaker: Unknown
en: It should be an agent that I can text, steer from Slack, or hear from wherever I am.
zh: 它应该是一个我可以发短信、从 Slack 引导，或者无论我在哪里都能听到的智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: Really, why can't I talk to my agent and have it design the whole loop for me?
zh: 真的，为什么我不能和我的智能体交谈并让它为我设计整个循环？

speaker: Unknown
en: We haven't solved that yet.
zh: 我们还没解决这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Models are advancing faster than the harnesses and organizations around them.
zh: 模型的进步速度超过了围绕它们的工具和组织。

speaker: Unknown
en: Designing those things
zh: 设计这些东西

speaker: Unknown
en: is the next engineering problem.
zh: 是下一个工程问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's where all of you come in.
zh: 这就是你们所有人的切入点。

speaker: Unknown
en: The future is not 20 terminals.
zh: 未来不是 20 个终端。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's better loops.
zh: 而是更好的循环。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's build them.
zh: 让我们来构建它们吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you.
zh: 谢谢。
